title: Symphony No. 9 in C major, “The Great”
hook: Shelved as too long in Schubert’s lifetime, it was rescued by Schumann, who loved its “heavenly length”.

painting.title: View of the Dachstein with the Hallstätter See from the Hütteneckalm near Ischl
painting.pairingNote: The lakes and peaks of Upper Austria, where Schubert spent the summer of 1825 working on the symphony, painted by a Viennese contemporary on the same broad, sunlit scale.

facts: Schubert worked on it in the summer of 1825, travelling through Upper Austria and the Alps, and had it fully scored by 1826. For a long time it was wrongly dated to 1828, his last year.

In October 1826 he sent it to Vienna’s Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde. Its amateur orchestra tried it through in 1827 and set it aside as too long and difficult. It was never properly performed in his lifetime.

In 1838, ten years after his death, Robert Schumann was shown the manuscript in Vienna by Schubert’s brother Ferdinand. Mendelssohn conducted the first full performance in Leipzig on 21 March 1839, and Schumann praised its “heavenly length”.
“The Great” first told it apart from Schubert’s shorter Symphony No. 6, also in C major. It is the same work sometimes numbered 7 or 8.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a horn call that grows into a journey (I), a march that breaks down (II), a huge dance (III), a whirlwind (IV).

movements.heading: Andante – Allegro ma non troppo
movements.summary: A slow introduction that begins with two horns alone, then a fast movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] driven by short, dotted rhythms. The horns’ opening tune comes back at the very end, played by the whole orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The horn tune
mainIdeas.description: a calm, eight-bar melody for two horns in [[unison|unison]], with no accompaniment.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a sharp, dotted figure in the strings, answered by the woodwinds in triplets.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, skipping tune for oboes and bassoons, in E minor instead of the expected G major.

stops.hear: Two horns alone play a long, calm tune
Other instruments take the tune up; it grows warmer and fuller
stops.happening: The introduction unfolds, almost a small movement of its own

stops.hear: The music grows louder and quicker and runs straight into the fast section
stops.happening: No pause between introduction and Allegro

stops.hear: Strings in a sharp, dotted rhythm; the woodwinds answer in triplets
Oboes and bassoons, quietly, a skipping tune in a minor key
The trombones, very softly, play a slow, solemn phrase
stops.happening: A melody for the trombones, recalling the horns’ opening tune

stops.hear: The trombone phrase and the dotted rhythm wander through new keys
The dotted Theme 1 returns at home in C major
Faster; the whole orchestra drives forward

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The horns’ opening tune, now broad and loud in the full orchestra
stops.happening: The introduction’s theme crowns the movement

notice: Listen to the trombones at ≈ 5:20. In Schubert’s time they mostly added weight to loud chords; here they play a quiet melody.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Judging by its length, Wand leaves out the exposition repeats here and in the finale, which keeps the symphony to about 52 minutes; with every repeat it lasts around an hour.

movements.heading: Andante con moto
movements.summary: A march in A minor with a lyrical second theme, each heard twice. The second time, the march builds to a crisis: loud, clashing chords, then complete silence.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a march tune for the oboe, with a jaunty dotted rhythm, over walking strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a warm, consoling melody in the strings, in F major.

stops.hear: Cellos and basses walk; then the oboe plays a march tune with a jaunty, dotted rhythm
The strings, softly, sing a warm, consoling melody
A horn repeats one soft note while the strings answer; the music seems to hold its breath
stops.happening: The way back to the march. Schumann wrote that the horn seems to call from another world while the orchestra listens

stops.hear: The oboe’s march again
The march builds to a climax of loud, repeated, clashing chords, then stops dead
stops.happening: The crisis of the movement, followed by silence

stops.hear: Cellos sing quietly, then plucked strings
The warm melody returns, now in A major

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: The march comes back, softer, and fades

notice: The silence after the climax (≈ 10:30) is part of the music. Count how long it lasts before anything moves again.

movements.heading: Scherzo. Allegro vivace
movements.summary: A huge [[scherzo|scherzo]] with a bouncing, rustic energy, and a [[trio|trio]] that is one of Schubert’s broadest melodies.

stops.hear: The strings, together, in a bouncing, stamping rhythm
Gentler: a swaying, waltz-like tune
stops.happening: The second idea, close to a [[landler|Ländler]]

stops.hear: The mood opens out: woodwinds sing a long, broad tune over a steady pulse in the strings
The stamping rhythm again
stops.happening: The scherzo returns, without its repeats

movements.heading: Finale. Allegro vivace
movements.summary: A long, relentless finale in [[sonata-form|sonata form]], built from galloping triplets and a theme of four repeated notes. Near its middle, a quiet tune close to Beethoven’s “Ode to Joy” slips past.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a fanfare-like call for the full orchestra, with galloping triplets in the strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: four repeated notes in the horns, then a dancing tune in the woodwinds over busy strings.

stops.hear: A loud call from the full orchestra; galloping triplets in the strings
Horns, softly, on four repeated notes; then a dancing woodwind tune over busy strings
Very quietly, the clarinets play a tune close to Beethoven’s “Ode to Joy”
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins with a nod to Beethoven’s Ninth

stops.hear: The opening call returns, in a surprising key
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]], starting in E-flat major instead of C

stops.label: Last 3 minutes
stops.hear: The four repeated notes grow from a whisper into hammer blows for the whole orchestra

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Every instrument hammers the same notes; a last, unison C

notice: Follow the four repeated notes from ≈ 1:45 to the end. They begin as a soft horn signal and finish as the climax of the whole symphony.
The story goes that in London in 1844 the violinists laughed at the second theme (≈ 1:45) in rehearsal, and the orchestra refused to play the symphony.

threads.title: Trombones as singers
threads.body: Schubert gives the trombones melodies, quiet ones as well as loud.

threads.title: Rhythm as engine
threads.body: Dotted figures, triplets and repeated notes drive all four movements.

threads.title: Beethoven’s shadow
threads.body: Schubert worked on it soon after Beethoven’s Ninth (1824), and the finale quotes it, briefly and almost in passing.
